prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a finished, extremely polished desktop WEB APP interface for BirdRadar, landscape 1536x1024. Edge-to-edge actual screen design, no computer device, no perspective frame, no marketing poster. First reference image is MATERIAL ONLY: luminous translucent milky silicone / latex film, cyan, lilac, ice blue, pale rose, thin gold fringes, silky microscopic line detail and transparent overlapping layers. Translate it into GEOGRAPHIC migration-density fields conforming to a real map, never a floating abstract sculpture. Second reference is existing bird stamp ART DIRECTION: perforated cream paper edge, dark botanical stamp, a bird as focal artwork. Upgrade stamp printing with prismatic Balatro-inspired holographic foil, embossed metallic outlines, tasteful diffraction and angle highlights; maintain bird identity and crisp typography. UI chrome is quiet matte midnight blue; reserve iridescence for the geographic heat field and stamps. Readable clean humanist sans typography, editorial serif for bird names, precise generous spacing. No neon cyberpunk, no generic dashboard card grid, no big metrics, no made-up live data. Keep coastline, relief and fine country/city labels readable THROUGH heat layers. The route core is denser/milkier, periphery semitransparent, overlapping ribbons form pale luminous interference. Some tiny flowing particles follow the corridor. Distinguish colours using a small legend. This is a conceptual visualization, not a scientific plot: include a clearly readable bottom note exactly "Concept preview · illustrative heat field". Real data provenance text can say "Historical tracking · Movebank". Main navigation: "BirdRadar" then "Explore", "Stamps", "Lights Out", "About". Every image must show a complete usable composition with species selector, map controls, timeline and stamp content. No watermark. COMPOSITION C — Follow one journey. Shared slim header and a distinct editorial exploration composition: LEFT 28% full-height matte near-black narrative rail with heading "Follow the white stork" in beautiful serif mixed with clean functional sans, subtitle "From Europe to West Africa". A minimalist vertical itinerary with three readable entries "Breeding grounds / Central Europe", "Autumn passage / Iberian Peninsula", "Wintering grounds / West Africa", with a September seasonal selection. An exquisite small 180x270mm-proportioned WHITE STORK perforated holographic stamp anchors the lower narrative rail, "View stamp" action. RIGHT 72% is an enormous close-scale, cropped ORTHOGRAPHIC GLOBE centred Europe and West Africa, deep blue relief, real geographic outlines, soft atmospheric edge, with transparent milky thin-film heat corridors hugging the Earth's surface from Germany through Spain to Senegal. The globe should fill its panel and remain map-like with place labels, not outer-space wallpaper. A dominant blue-lilac translucent route membrane has multiple flowing folds and a concentrated core, one peach branch, silky striations at edges. Minimal map zoom controls on right and a horizontal season scrubber integrated at bottom. A small foldout layer control upper-right "Density / Tracks / Observations" with Density selected. Note exactly "Concept preview · illustrative heat field" below the map. It feels contemplative, tactile and scientifically curious; route geography, stamp foil and migration story form one understandable product, not unrelated decoration.
